newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SOCCER-INTER ADVANCE DESPITE INCE DISMISSAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER ADVANCE DESPITE INCE DISMISSAL.

text.p: Ten-man Inter-Milan reached the third round of the UEFA Cup by squeezing past Casino Graz 5-3 on penalties on Tuesday after having England international midfielder Paul Ince sent off in extra time.
The Austrians, who only lost the first leg 1-0 against their more illustrious opponents, wiped out that deficit in the 35th minute when Herfried Sabitzer levelled the tie from the penalty spot.
There were no more goals and the match was eventually decided by penalties after Inter had been reduced to 10 men following Ince's 95th-minute sending off for his second yellow card of the night.
Ince was first booked in the 62nd minute for arguing with French referee Gilles Veissiere and was shown the yellow again and sent off for a heavy foul on Dieter Ramusch.
It was the second red card for Ince in just over two weeks following his dismissal in an Italian league match against Piacenza on October 13.
On that occasion Ince was sent off for felling an opponent waiting for a corner after the opponent, Gianpietro Piovani, apparantly racially insulted him.

While Ince was cast as the villain of the night, Inter's goalie Gianluca Pagliuca kept his cool in the shootout and made the decisive save from Erwin Dampfhofer that set up the victory. Salvatore Fresi sealed it by converting his penalty to make it 5-3. Graz dominated the first half, with Sabitzer missing two chances in the sixth and 12th minutes on the wet and slippery pitch.

Inter's attempts at securing the tie were all thwarted by 19-year-old goalkeeper Alexander Manninger, who had another excellent match following an ooutstaning performance in the first leg in only his second appearance in a European cup tie.
